questions.prompt: In our 1,000-person world, how many commercial flights take off today?
questions.hint: About 102,000 flights depart globally every day.
questions.followUpIntro: Those flights carry a lot of fuel. Let's follow the chain...

questions.prompt: Of those 10 flights in our world, how many passengers do they carry in total?
questions.hint: A typical commercial flight carries 150–200 passengers.
questions.followUpIntro: All that travel has a carbon cost...

questions.prompt: How much CO₂ does our 1,000-person world emit per year from all sources?
questions.hint: Think about 4.6 tonnes per person × 1,000 people.
questions.followUpIntro: Now let's zoom out to the whole world...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people work in farming, fishing, or forestry?
questions.hint: In developing nations the share is much higher than in wealthy ones.
questions.followUpIntro: Those farmers need land. How much?

questions.prompt: How many calories per day are available to each person in our world?
questions.hint: The world actually produces more than enough food for everyone.
questions.followUpIntro: But not all food makes it to the table...

questions.prompt: How many tonnes of food does our 1,000-person world waste each year?
questions.hint: About one-third of all food produced globally is wasted.
questions.followUpIntro: Hunger persists despite this abundance...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people live on less than $2.15 a day?
questions.hint: Poverty — not food scarcity — is the main driver of hunger.
questions.followUpIntro: This is the heart of global food inequality.

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people lack safe drinking water?
questions.hint: This is still one of humanity's biggest solvable problems.
questions.followUpIntro: Those without clean water face daily risks. But even those who have it use it unequally...

questions.prompt: How many liters of freshwater does the average person use per day?
questions.hint: This includes drinking, cooking, sanitation, and agriculture. Americans use ~500L.
questions.followUpIntro: Water access is closely tied to electricity access...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people have no access to electricity?
questions.hint: Without power, pumping clean water is much harder.
questions.followUpIntro: Infrastructure deprivation compounds itself.

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people are children under 15?
questions.hint: About 1 in 4 people globally is under 15.
questions.followUpIntro: Those children need teachers...

questions.prompt: How many primary school teachers serve our 1,000-person world?
questions.hint: Average class sizes globally are around 24 students.
questions.followUpIntro: But not all children reach a classroom...

questions.prompt: How many children in our 1,000-person world are not in school?
questions.hint: Progress has been huge, but exclusion persists in the most vulnerable communities.
questions.followUpIntro: Literacy shows us the legacy of past exclusion...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 adults can read and write?
questions.hint: Global literacy has improved dramatically but illiteracy is still concentrated in specific regions.
questions.followUpIntro: Literacy unlocks digital access...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people have access to the internet?
questions.hint: Connectivity requires both infrastructure and the skills to use it.
questions.followUpIntro: The internet is the great equalizer — when you can reach it.

questions.prompt: What is the average annual income per person in our 1,000-person world (in USD)?
questions.hint: The global average hides huge variation — the median is much lower.
questions.followUpIntro: But averages can be misleading when wealth is concentrated...

questions.prompt: Out of every 1,000 units of global wealth, how many does the richest 10% hold?
questions.hint: Wealth inequality is far more extreme than income inequality.
questions.followUpIntro: This concentration has real consequences...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people survive on under $2.15 a day?
questions.hint: Extreme poverty has fallen dramatically but remains concentrated in specific regions.
questions.followUpIntro: Poverty and lack of shelter go hand in hand...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people live in inadequate housing or slums?
questions.hint: Rapid urbanization has outpaced housing construction in many cities.
questions.followUpIntro: Housing, income, water — the deprivations cluster together.

questions.prompt: How many doctors serve our 1,000-person world?
questions.hint: Global average is 4.3 doctors per 1,000 — but inequality is enormous.
questions.followUpIntro: Doctors need nurses and midwives to support them...

questions.prompt: How many nurses and midwives work in our 1,000-person world?
questions.hint: There are typically 2–3 nurses for every doctor globally.
questions.followUpIntro: Even with healthcare workers, access depends on clean water...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people lack safe drinking water?
questions.hint: Waterborne disease is one of the biggest killers preventable through clean water.
questions.followUpIntro: Health outcomes show up in life expectancy...

questions.prompt: What is the average life expectancy in our 1,000-person world (in years)?
questions.hint: Global life expectancy has risen dramatically — from 48 in 1950 to 73 today.
questions.followUpIntro: The world is aging as it gets healthier.

questions.prompt: How many kg of CO₂ does the average person emit per year?
questions.hint: This average hides a 30× gap between richest and poorest countries.
questions.followUpIntro: Cars are a major source of emissions...

questions.prompt: How many cars are there in our 1,000-person world?
questions.hint: The US has 800 cars per 1,000 people — but that's far above the global average.
questions.followUpIntro: Alongside carbon, forests are the other half of the equation...

questions.prompt: How many hectares of forest does our 1,000-person world lose per year?
questions.hint: 47 million hectares lost globally — an area the size of Sweden.
questions.followUpIntro: Renewables offer hope...

questions.prompt: Out of every 1,000 kWh of electricity generated, how many come from renewable sources?
questions.hint: Wind, solar, hydro, and other renewables are growing fast.
questions.followUpIntro: The transition is underway — but uneven.

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people own a smartphone?
questions.hint: Smartphones have spread faster than any technology in history.
questions.followUpIntro: Smartphones need internet to be truly useful...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people have internet access?
questions.hint: Slightly fewer than smartphone owners — some have phones but no data plan.
questions.followUpIntro: Internet access matters most to those who can read...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 adults can read and write?
questions.hint: Literacy is the gateway to using digital technology effectively.
questions.followUpIntro: Urban areas drive connectivity...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people live in cities?
questions.hint: Urban areas have far better connectivity than rural ones.
questions.followUpIntro: The digital divide tracks the urban-rural divide.

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people are forcibly displaced — refugees or displaced within their own country?
questions.hint: This figure hit a record high in 2023 and is still rising.
questions.followUpIntro: Displacement disrupts children's education...

questions.prompt: How many children in our 1,000-person world are not in school?
questions.hint: Children in conflict zones are many times more likely to be out of school.
questions.followUpIntro: Displacement and poverty are deeply linked...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people live in extreme poverty?
questions.hint: Conflict is one of the biggest drivers of poverty.
questions.followUpIntro: The world keeps moving — in more ways than one.

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people are over 65 years old?
questions.hint: This proportion will roughly double by 2050 as the global population ages.
questions.followUpIntro: An aging population needs more healthcare workers...

questions.prompt: How many doctors serve our 1,000-person world?
questions.hint: Demand for doctors will grow as populations age.
questions.followUpIntro: An aging world also means fewer children relative to adults...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people are under 15 years old?
questions.hint: The ratio of young to old is shifting — with profound economic consequences.
questions.followUpIntro: Life expectancy captures this whole story...

questions.prompt: What is the global average life expectancy in years?
questions.hint: It rose from 48 years in 1950 to 73 today.
questions.followUpIntro: A longer-lived world is a richer, more complex world.

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people have no access to electricity?
questions.hint: This number has fallen from 120 per 1,000 in 2010 to under 75 today.
questions.followUpIntro: Those with electricity use very different amounts...

questions.prompt: How many kWh of electricity does the average person use per year?
questions.hint: Americans use ~12,000 kWh; Ethiopians use ~100 kWh.
questions.followUpIntro: Where does all that electricity come from?

questions.prompt: Out of every 1,000 kWh of electricity generated globally, how many come from renewables?
questions.hint: Wind, solar, and hydro are all growing fast.
questions.followUpIntro: Energy use is closely tied to carbon emissions...

questions.prompt: How many kg of CO₂ does the average person emit per year?
questions.hint: Energy use is the biggest driver of CO₂ emissions.
questions.followUpIntro: The energy transition will reshape this number.

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people live in cities?
questions.hint: For the first time in history, over half of humanity is urban.
questions.followUpIntro: Cities concentrate cars and transportation...

questions.prompt: How many cars are there in our 1,000-person world?
questions.hint: Cars are concentrated in cities and wealthy suburbs.
questions.followUpIntro: Urban growth also creates housing pressure...

questions.prompt: How many of our 1,000 people live in inadequate housing?
questions.hint: Rapid urbanization has outpaced affordable housing in many developing cities.
questions.followUpIntro: Better housing brings better health...

questions.prompt: What is the average global life expectancy in years?
questions.hint: Urban dwellers tend to live longer than rural ones on average.
questions.followUpIntro: The urban century is reshaping everything.
